subject: How to fit mixed effect model in NIMBLE

messages.author: 0be29200f0a7e1a9
messages.subject: How to fit mixed effect model in NIMBLE
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am a new user to NIMBLE. I am trying to fit a mixed effects model. However, I don't know how to write the correct code

my try:

for (i in 1:N) {
# for i th subject
# they may have different number of clustered observations
    for (j in s[i]:e[i]) {
      EM[j] <- (beta[L[i], 1])  + Time[j]*beta[L[i], 2] + b0[i] * sigma_b 
      M[j] ~ dnorm(EM[j], sd = sigma_M)
    }
  }

I can run this code but always have the warning message: [Warning] Multiple definitions for the same node.
            Did you forget indexing with 'i' on the left-hand side of
            `M[j] ~ dnorm(mean = EM[j], sd = sigma_M, lower_ = -Inf, upper_ = Inf, .tau = sigma_M^-2, .var = sigma_M * sigma_M)`?

Thanks,
Jun

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: How to fit mixed effect model in NIMBLE
parts:
Jun, thanks for your question, and your use of nimble.

As the warning message suggests (" [Warning] Multiple definitions for the same node.  Did you forget indexing with 'i' on the left-hand side of   `M[j] ~ dnorm ...."), the issue you're encountering is that the declaration for M[j] is enclosed (not only inside the loop over j, but also) inside the loop over i.  So, for each pair of values {i,j}, nimble attempts to create a "new" node in the model defined by M[j].  However, if i takes on multiple values, this results in (attempting to) create M[j] multiple times, which is not allowed.

This can be fixed, but adding indexing over i as well, for the EM and M variables:

for(i in 1:N) {

# for i th subject
# they may have different number of clustered observations

for(j in s[i]:e[i]) {
      EM[i,j] <- (beta[L[i], 1]) + Time[j]*beta[L[i], 2] + b0[i] * sigma_b
      M[i,j] ~ dnorm(EM[i,j], sd = sigma_M)
    }
  }

Assuming everything else with your model is correct (priors, the specification of Time, L, etc), this should hopefully get you going.

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.author: 20690f23c3a86c45
messages.subject: Re: How to fit mixed effect model in NIMBLE
parts:
You are getting this error because your EM and M variables are in two embedded loops.
With your current structure they should be indexed such as EM[i,j] and M[i,j]

G
